To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the finite precision on initial conditions and on the evolution law are equivalent in the sense that they lead to the same finite time predictability; and (ii) the statistical properties are insensitive to the finite precision in the evolution law.

the round-off error in the initial conditions of a chaotic system is equivalent to the round-off error of the equations of motion and that the round-off errors in the initial conditions or in the equations of motion do not change the statistical properties of the system.

the predictability time tp of the chaotic dynamics is the same in the presence of a perturbation of the dynamics and in the case of the finite precision in the knowledge of initial conditions, and that the statistical properties of a chaotic system are not sensitive to a perturbation of evolution law or to the finite precision in initial conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of uncertainty on the knowledge of a dynamical system on the statistical properties of the system.
the effect of uncertainty on the evolution of dynamical systems.
the effects of a small perturbation on the evolution law of a dynamical system, in particular on chaotic dynamical systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the roundoff effects and the finite precision in the initial conditions can not be distinguished in the statistical properties of chaotic dynamical system.
the roundoff error is a perturbation on the evolution law, which has a negligible influence on the statistical properties, except for the short predictability.
the finite precision in the knowledge of the system evolution law or initial state is not important for statistical properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the predictability time tp of the evolution law is not a fundamental limit for the predictability of the statistical properties of chaotic systems, at least in the case of short time correlations.
the predictability time is the only relevant time scale for the statistical properties of chaotic dynamical system.
, if we are not interested in the predictability time of a single trajectory, we can safely use a slightly wrong model to predict the long time behaviour.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the predictability of chaotic systems is not a problem for the statistical description of the dynamics, which is robust with respect to small changes in both the evolution law and in the initial conditions.
a finite precision in the knowledge of the evolution law or in the initial conditions can be considered as a small perturbation in the dynamics.
, for a given precision, the predictability time is the same for chaotic and integrable systems.
